supercharger_access.notes: Quick web lookup. Canadian article (Sept 2024) on the GM NACS adapter for Canadian owners of Blazer EV, Equinox EV, Silverado EV and LYRIQ. Says nothing about 2026 trim ports.

US page: CCS1 cars use Superchargers with the GM-approved NACS adapter ($299) / optional adapter in GM's spec guide. Current state for model year 2026: adapter needed. Markets: CA/US. (2026 car: same port and adapter state as the 2025 car on this model.)

consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, mid-80s F (~29 C), climate 70 F low fan, wheel size not stated, battery-side (car display) | 2024 Equinox EV FWD 2RS (same generation and 85 kWh pack as our 2026 FWD). Car reported 90.2 kWh used over 303 mi (3.4 mi/kWh): 90.2 kWh / 303 mi = 297.7 Wh/mi / 1.609344 = 185 Wh/km. Hot weather with A/C load. Other tests seen: Consumer Reports AWD 304 mi at 70 mph (no energy figure, paywalled).

charge_port.notes: CCS1 (J1772 native inlet) through the 2026 model year: press pages for this model line state CCS1 for 2024-2026 and NACS from 2027. Same port assumed for the Canadian car (Guide Auto 2024-09-18: Canadian owners need the GM adapter). Model year 2026. (2026 car: same port and adapter state as the 2025 car on this model.)
